skill.name: reviewing-code
skill.description: Guides AI-assisted code review with validation commands, review sections, project checks, and a clear approval format.
skill.summary: Provides a structured workflow for reviewing code changes and pull requests.
skill.author: BPSAI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. One command pattern uses xargs over changed filenames and should be made safer before broad publication.

remediation.issue: Unsafe xargs pipeline over changed filenames
remediation.suggestion: Use null-delimited paths and explicit option termination, such as git diff -z with xargs -0 and grep --.

finding_verdicts.reason: The flagged text is an opening Markdown code fence, not Ruby backtick execution. The commands inside are hardcoded review helpers, not dynamic code evaluation.
The flagged text is a closing Markdown code fence. It does not execute a command or define executable source code.
The flagged text starts a Markdown example block for the review output format. It is documentation text, not shell or Ruby execution.
The flagged text is the closing fence for a Markdown template. No executable command or backtick evaluation is present.
The flagged text is a Markdown bash fence, not a Ruby backtick operator. The actual command risk is covered separately by the xargs finding.
The xargs pipeline processes repository-controlled filenames without null delimiters or grep option termination. This is not arbitrary command text, but it can mis-handle crafted filenames.

medium_findings.title: xargs command (can execute arbitrary commands)
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The xargs pipeline processes repository-controlled filenames without null delimiters or grep option termination. This is not arbitrary command text, but it can mis-handle crafted filenames.

content.user_title: Review Code Changes with Structured Feedback
content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss risks when feedback is unstructured. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a repeatable review checklist and verdict format.
actual_capabilities: Suggests validation commands for tests, linting, structure checks, and diffs.
Defines a clear review output with summary, required fixes, suggestions, and verdict.
Checks for type hints, docstrings, hardcoded values, and new test coverage.
Highlights project-specific needs, including mocked Trello and GitHub API calls.
Provides quick checks for debug statements, TODO markers, and likely secrets.
limitations: Does not make final merge decisions for maintainers.
Requires access to the repository diff for accurate findings.
Command examples may need adjustment for non-Git workflows.
Does not replace security scanning or full test execution.

use_cases.title: Pull Request Review
use_cases.description: Review a change set with required fixes, suggestions, positive notes, and an approval recommendation.

use_cases.title: Quality Gate Check
use_cases.description: Check whether a branch includes tests, documentation, type hints, and project-specific safeguards.

use_cases.title: Pre-Submit Self Review
use_cases.description: Run a structured pass before requesting review so common issues are resolved earlier.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when reviewing a small change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current code changes. Summarize the impact, list must-fix issues, and give an approval verdict.

prompt_templates.title: Pull Request Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when preparing feedback on a pull request.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this pull request against the skill checklist. Separate must-fix issues, should-fix items, optional improvements, and positive notes.

prompt_templates.title: Release Readiness Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before merging a larger feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this branch for release readiness. Focus on tests, configuration, external service mocking, secrets, and maintainability.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture and Risk Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for complex changes with broader impact.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the design and implementation risks in this change. Identify behavioral regressions, missing safeguards, and long-term maintenance concerns.

output_examples.input: A pull request adds GitHub API integration without tests for failed responses.
output_examples.output: Must fix: add failure-path tests for API errors. Should fix: document retry behavior. Verdict: request changes.

output_examples.input: A branch refactors utility functions and adds type hints.
output_examples.output: Summary: the refactor is clear and covered by tests. Consider adding docstrings for public helpers. Verdict: approve with comments.

output_examples.input: A change introduces configuration values directly inside application logic.
output_examples.output: Must fix: move hardcoded values into configuration. Should fix: add tests for missing configuration. Verdict: request changes.

best_practices: Run the relevant checks before asking for a final review verdict.
Review the diff and surrounding code before writing findings.
Keep feedback specific, actionable, and tied to file locations when possible.
anti_patterns: Approving changes before tests, linting, or project checks are considered.
Mixing optional preferences with required correctness or security fixes.
Reporting generic issues without evidence from the changed code.

faq.question: What does this skill help review?
faq.answer: It helps review code changes, pull requests, quality checks, tests, documentation, and maintainability concerns.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It suggests useful commands, but the agent or user must decide whether to run them.

faq.question: Can it approve a pull request?
faq.answer: It can recommend a verdict, but maintainers should make the final merge decision.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What project checks does it emphasize?
faq.answer: It emphasizes tests, type hints, docstrings, configuration usage, mocked services, and existing project patterns.

faq.question: Is it a security scanner?
faq.answer: No. It can flag likely secrets and risky changes, but dedicated scanners are still needed.
